purpose: Primary-source experimental references for corrugated-board crease formation and post-crease bending, with explicit specimen, tooling, loading, and observables. Values labelled digitized or derived are not raw source tables.

sources.citation: Nagasawa, S. and Komiyama, Y. (2012). Effect of Scoring Condition on Creasing Characteristics of Double-Wall Corrugated Board. Journal of Advanced Mechanical Design, Systems, and Manufacturing 6(7), 1263-1272. DOI: 10.1299/jamdsm.6.1263.

board.architecture: AB double-wall corrugated fiberboard, outside to inside nominal sheet basis weights 210(K6)-160-160-180-210(K6) g/m^2
board.caution: The five-sheet flat calipers sum to 1.17 mm; this is not assembled board caliper. AB double-wall construction and paper grades differ from the single-wall Haj-Ali 2009 recipe.

raw_paper_tensile_table_1.condition: 50% RH, 296 K, strain rate 0.002 s^-1; values are ultimate tensile stress, breaking strain, and Young modulus, not yield/hardening tables

scoring_machine.arrangement: three parallel scoring lines: a pre-creaser pair followed by a main-creaser pair; center line measured, side lines are dummy stabilizers

main_creaser.flat_anvil: 8 mm width, 7 mm thick urethane rubber insert, JIS K-6253 hardness 90

scoring_machine.failure_metric: inside-liner failure occurrence q; counted as a failure when the combined failure-zone length exceeded 5% of specimen length. The authors report actually observed failure lengths often exceeded half the specimen.
scoring_machine.replicates: 10 specimens for failure occurrence and 10 for bending per creaser-gap condition; Fig.9 describes 10 pieces from two 230x320 blanks.

process_conditions.conditioning: specimens held 24 h in room conditions averaging 296 K and 50% RH for the stated reference condition

moisture_sensitivity.observation: The authors report that a 1.6 percentage-point increase in board water content reduced inside-liner failure occurrence by about 20-40%; Fig.12 shows the dependence on pre-creaser gap.

best_gap_observations: With main gap cC=0.7 mm and V=2.92 m/s, the local minimum in inside-liner failures occurs near pre-gap cP/t=0.15-0.25.
With no pre-creasing, q rises markedly for main gap cC/t<0.4 and is about 1 at cC/t=0.09.
With no main crease, q rises for pre-gap cP/t<0.09.

fold_reference.instrument: prototype crease stress test measuring bending line moment per unit width against rotation angle
fold_reference.available_numeric_curve_data: Figure 9 plots the moment-angle response from 10 pieces from two blanks; there is no raw point table in the article. Figure 10 gives measured peak moment versus crease/flute-apex offset. No digitized moment-angle samples are included in this manifest.

peak_moment_offset_relation.delta_x_definition: ΔX=e/λ, crease displacement from flute apex divided by flute pitch
peak_moment_offset_relation.status: equation printed in article Eq.1; not a fit reconstructed here

unreported_for_this_source: adhesive formulation, bondline dimensions, adhesive density, cohesive strength, or fracture energy
crease crack-initiation stress or fracture-energy calibration

sources.citation: Aduke, R. N., Venter, M. P., and Coetzee, C. J. (2024). Numerical Modelling of Corrugated Paperboard Boxes. Mathematics and Computation in Applied Sciences 29(4), 70. DOI: 10.3390/mca29040070.

evidence_pages.material_and_crease_models: Printed pp.7-8, Tables 1-2; p.10, Table 3; pp.14-16, Tables 4-5 and Figs.14-15.
evidence_pages.availability: Article states data are available from authors on request; plotted curves are not provided as tabular raw samples.

board.conditioning: 23 °C, 50% RH for 24 h under BS EN 20187:1993

yield_stress_table_3_MPa.provenance: Reported as yield values used in the study, sourced by the article to Cillie and Coetzee (2022), rather than a new sheet test in this 2024 work.

physical_creased_four_point_bend.crease_position: center of specimen, across the specimen; source describes the sample as creased with fluting oriented in CD
physical_creased_four_point_bend.deflection_sensor: HBM WA100 100 mm LVDT measuring at the crease center
physical_creased_four_point_bend.stop_rule: record until failure; stop when force drops 10% from maximum

quantitative_targets.creased_to_uncreased_stiffness_ratio_sta: admitted as a dimensionless rounded within-study comparison derived from the source-reported 63% reduction; it does not depend on resolving the absolute unit convention

equation_1_variable_definitions_as_print.Y: maximum deflection at the sample centre
equation_1_variable_definitions_as_print.a: distance between supporting and loading anvils, 70 mm

quantitative_targets.equation_1_dimensional_result_if_lengths: N*m: (P/Y) has units N/m, (L^3/b) has units m^2, and (a/L) is dimensionless
quantitative_targets.table_5_equation_unit_mismatch: Table 5 caption prints N/m, but Eq. 1 as printed has dimensions force times length when P is a force and Y,L,a,b are lengths. The article does not resolve the mismatch; do not silently correct the published unit.
quantitative_targets.absolute_stiffness_target_admission: not admitted for quantitative model comparison until the authors or cited Eq. 1 source clarify the unit/convention; retain 6.88 only as the value and N/m label printed in Table 5
quantitative_targets.derived_status: 6.88*(1-0.63); rounded estimate, not directly tabulated. Its absolute unit inherits the unresolved Table 5 / Eq. 1 mismatch and it is not an admitted quantitative target. The 0.37 ratio remains an admissible rounded dimensionless report.

curves.Figure_15: experimental force-displacement curves for creased and uncreased CD four-point bends are plotted

physical_creased_four_point_bend.crease_creation_boundary: The paper describes the post-crease bending tests but does not report the creasing rule/channel geometry, score gap/depth, crease feed speed, score load, crease moisture content, or the process used to create these physical creases.

structural_FE_crease_zone.status: approximated from physical crease width for FE calibration, not a complete crease-tool geometry
structural_FE_crease_zone.status_of_properties: inverse-calibrated FE crease-zone inputs; do not treat as directly measured constituent paper properties

equivalent_homogenized_creaseregion_para.status: inverse-calibrated homogenized FE material parameters for this board and bending setup; not a direct local material measurement

adhesive_and_failure_boundary.FE_liner_medium_joint: structural model connects liner and flute-tip nodes directly; perfect kinematic bond assumption
adhesive_and_failure_boundary.adhesive_modulus_density_fracture_or_cur: not supplied for this grade; authors note that real starch-bond flexibility may further reduce FE stiffness
adhesive_and_failure_boundary.local_paper_damage_law: crease region is represented by inverse-calibrated reduced properties; the physical score tool and local damage history are not identified

nontransferable_related_source.citation: Beex, L. A. A. and Peerlings, R. H. J. (2009). An experimental and computational study of laminated paperboard creasing and folding. International Journal of Solids and Structures 46, 4192-4207.
nontransferable_related_source.reason_not_a_corrugated_board_benchmark: Solid laminated paperboard, with no corrugated medium/flute-and-liner geometry. Its layer delamination and crease response can inform possible mechanisms but its material and force-angle data cannot validate a corrugated board recipe.

raw_curve_data_status.nagasawa_2012: Moment-angle is Figure 9 only; peak-moment offset relationship is Eq.1. No raw numeric moment-angle table or supplementary time series found.
raw_curve_data_status.aduke_2024: Four-point force-displacement is Figure 15 only; Table 5 prints uncreased stiffness in N/m while Eq. 1 dimensions are force times length, an unresolved source unit mismatch. Prose gives a rounded 63% decrease, supporting the dimensionless 0.37 ratio but not an absolute stiffness target. Article says raw data are available from authors on request.
raw_curve_data_status.digitization: No graph points were digitized for this package; only the clearly labelled derived stiffness estimate is calculated from a table value and the source's rounded percentage.
